title: Netflix Is So Hot Because It Gives Us What We Want: TV
summary: Netflix's stock is experiencing significant growth due to the public's love for TV and the company's ability to provide content cheaply, easily, and without ads. The article highlights Netflix's impressive subscriber numbers and competitive edge against traditional media and other streaming services, further boosted by an upcoming stock split. Analysts credit Netflix's success to its consumer-first approach, technological investments, and substantial spending on compelling original content.

title: Walmart planning massive $200 M distribution center in Polk County
summary: Walmart is planning a massive $200 million distribution center in Polk County, Florida, which will include two giant warehouses in the Davenport area. This project is expected to bring hundreds of jobs to the region, pending approval of millions in tax abatements from Polk commissioners.

title: Gartner’s 2015 Cloud Storage Magic Quadrant: Our Key Takeaways
summary: Gartner's 2015 Magic Quadrant for Public Cloud Storage Services highlights Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, and Google as market leaders, dominating smaller vendors like Verizon, Rackspace, IBM, and AT&T, which are relegated to niche markets. The report provides insights into the "hyperscale vendors'" strategies, including Google's aggressive pricing and Microsoft's strong infrastructure, while also noting criticisms such as AWS's complex pricing. It underscores the intense competition and evolving landscape of the cloud storage market.

title: Kroger; an attractive long-term investment
summary: This article presents Kroger as an attractive long-term investment due to its consistent performance, strategic market expansion through diverse store formats and acquisitions, and focus on customer loyalty and shareholder value. The company, primarily operating in the US, aims for 11% annual earnings growth, supported by share buybacks, dividends, and new business investments. Its past performance, including a 242.9% total return over three years, compares favorably to the S&P 500.

title: Microsoft to cut 7,800 more jobs; writes off $7.6 billion in Nokia deal
summary: Microsoft announced a major restructuring of its mobile devices business, writing off $7.6 billion from its Nokia acquisition and cutting 7,800 jobs globally, primarily in its phone segment. This marks the second round of significant job cuts under CEO Satya Nadella, as the company shifts its strategy from a standalone phone business to growing a vibrant Windows ecosystem. Microsoft aims to narrow its focus to three key customer segments and run a more effective, narrower phone portfolio.

title: ODM Storage Vendors Gain Share From Giants: EMC, HP, IBM, NetApp Lose Market Presence
summary: Traditional storage systems manufacturers like EMC, NetApp, HP, and IBM are losing market share to low-cost original design manufacturer (ODM) storage vendors, a trend mirroring the server market due to the shift towards cloud computing and large data centers. This change is driven by customers preferring "white-box" solutions and a general decline in worldwide spending on information storage, leading to decreased revenues for larger players while smaller and mid-range vendors see gains. The article details how each major vendor has been impacted, including their revenue declines and strategies to adapt to the evolving market.

title: These are some of Amazon's Prime Day deals
summary: Amazon is previewing some of its Prime Day deals ahead of the sale, which is scheduled in honor of the retail giant's 20th anniversary. Deals include significant discounts on various TV sizes, Amazon's Fire TV stick, and Kindle e-readers. Amazon claims the Prime Day sale, which is exclusive to Prime members, will rival Black Friday in terms of the number of deals.

title: Amazon Prime Day Deals: Everything You Need to Know About Prime Day
summary: Amazon launched its first-ever Prime Day on July 15, 2015, offering significant deals on thousands of items to its Prime members. This event, described as "Christmas in July," aimed to boost Prime memberships, which had already seen substantial growth. The article also details the positive impact on Amazon's stock leading up to and during Prime Day, with an analyst upgrade and increased price targets.

title: Amazon Stock Price Today, on Prime Day's Debut (Nasdaq: AMZN)
summary: Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN) debuted its first-ever "Prime Day" on July 15, 2015, a 24-hour sale event promising more deals than Black Friday, which was expected to impact the stock price. Ahead of Prime Day, AMZN stock hit a record intraday high of $465.95, closing up 2.2% at $465.57 and showing a 50.01% year-to-date gain. UBS analyst Eric Sheridan upgraded Amazon to "Buy" and boosted his price target to $550, citing the increasing importance of Prime subscribers.

title: Twitter users: Prime Day a bad 'garage sale'
summary: Amazon's Prime Day, intended to celebrate its 20th birthday, was met with widespread disappointment from Twitter users who likened the sales event to a "garage sale." Customers complained about the underwhelming assortment of discounted merchandise, including items like granny panties and an extra-long shoehorn. Rivals like Walmart capitalized on the discontent by launching their own sales and criticizing Amazon's Prime-member-only approach.

title: MicroStrategy Secure Cloud™ Now Generally Available
summary: MicroStrategy announced the general availability of MicroStrategy Secure Cloud, allowing organizations to deploy enterprise analytics applications in minutes. This new cloud offering combines MicroStrategy 10 Secure Enterprise features with Amazon Web Services' scalable infrastructure, providing a fully configured, multi-tier analytics environment. The service aims to offer rapid deployment, scalability, security, and cost-effectiveness for enterprise analytics and mobile applications.

title: PayPal makes big splash on first day of trading after eBay spinoff
summary: On its first day of trading as an independent public company, PayPal's market value reached nearly $49 billion, surpassing its former parent company eBay. This move followed pressure from activist investor Carl Icahn for eBay to spin off PayPal. PayPal's shares rose 5.4%, while eBay's gained 2.4%, reflecting their divergent growth paths, with PayPal showing strong revenue and transaction volume increases compared to eBay's challenges.

title: TripAdvisor hopes lavish new headquarters in Needham will boost hiring
summary: TripAdvisor has opened a lavish new 282,000-square-foot headquarters in Needham, designed with amenities like a fitness center, game room, and free lunches, hoping to attract top tech talent in a competitive market. The company currently has 100 open positions and designed the office to enable employees to be social and active, though recruiters have mixed opinions on how much office environment alone drives hiring. The town of Needham offered TripAdvisor $1.8 million in reduced taxes over 13 years to attract the company.

title: Could Groupon be headed for the auction block?
summary: Groupon's consistently falling stock price, despite recent performance improvements, has led an analyst to suggest the company might consider selling itself. With controlling shareholders wielding significant power, a sale to potential buyers like Google or Amazon could offer a way out of its valuation woes, especially if upcoming earnings don't boost investor confidence. The decision ultimately rests with CEO Eric Lefkofsky, who has substantial voting control.

title: Walmart takes on Target in the baby aisle
summary: Walmart is significantly expanding its baby product offerings, directly challenging Target in a critical product category. This move aims to attract millennial mothers, a demographic responsible for 90% of new mothers in the U.S. Both retailers are vying for a larger share of the $1 trillion spent annually by parents on their children.

title: HP buys Stackato to beef up cloud development
summary: Hewlett-Packard (HPQ) is acquiring Stackato, a platform-as-a-service product from its long-time partner ActiveState, to bolster its hybrid cloud strategy. This acquisition strengthens HP's Helion portfolio and commitment to open-source solutions amidst its ongoing corporate overhaul and struggles in the public cloud market. HP will position Stackato to boost its hybrid cloud worldview, which focuses on integrating on-premise systems with external cloud services.

title: OIP Technologies, Inc. v. Amazon.com, Inc. - Price Optimization in E-Commerce Not Patent Eligible
authors: ['Intellectual Property Practice Group', 'McDermott Will & Schulte LLP - IP Update Blog']
summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit affirmed a district court's decision that a patent on price optimization in e-commerce does not claim eligible subject matter under 35 U.S.C. § 101, following the Supreme Court’s Alice decision. The court found that OIP Technologies' patent on a computer-implemented price optimization method merely described an abstract idea and conventional computer activities, thus failing to transform into patent-eligible subject matter. Judge Mayer's concurring opinion emphasized that patent eligibility is an issue properly resolved at the pleading stage to conserve judicial resources.

title: Smart Beta: Single Factor vs. Multi-Factor Approaches
summary: The article discusses the differences between single-factor and multi-factor smart beta ETFs, which combine passive and active investing approaches. It explains how single-factor funds focus on one characteristic like value or momentum, while multi-factor funds combine several factors using proprietary algorithms. The piece also compares their performance and considerations like expense ratios and turnover, noting that while single-factor funds can outperform if the right factor is chosen, multi-factor funds may offer more consistent benchmark-beating performance over time.
